hub.speaker: A Shepherd
hub.text: Wolf sign's thicker every week. Three lambs gone since spring. The pack's off its own ground and eating mine.

text_variants.text: Dark soon. Field edge, when you're ready. I'll be there.
You stood a watch before I ever asked. Word went round the fields.
Didn't figure we'd both still be standing after that. Sit at my fire any night you like.
Count's holding. Fires stay lit till thaw anyway.

options._comment: #396: REPLACES the come-along ask IN PLACE (cursor-pin rule). Same frozen counter, same semantics: this NPC fields as ally at river_wolf_pack.
options.text: [Offer to stand the night watch with him.]

options._comment: REPORT ROWS all carry heard_thicket_keeps beside their route counter: hut_ward_scrap has no quest-start gate, so a mage PC could read the scrap on a wander and settle thicket_answered for a quest never offered, firing 'New quest'/'Quest complete' back to back. Stated on all three so a later ungated producer cannot leak either.
options.text: The line's a ward. An old one, gone sour.
Fences are moved. The herd's got its road.
The den's empty. Whatever it was.

options._comment: R2 TALK-route RE-ENTRY, APPENDED LAST so cursor-pinned canonicals keep their indices. The start row is hide_when heard_thicket_keeps, the counter it banks, so thicket_brief/thicket_sign (herd_rerouted, the whole TALK route, and the hut pointer) were reachable only inside the accept conversation; leaving early orphaned them permanently while the beat still read 'Read the sign with the hunter'. Tallyman shape: requires the quest, hides on the route's terminal counter.
options.text: Take me back to that line in the thicket.

options._comment: #396 OFFER. Ungated (ruling 3, untied); hide_when its own counter so it is one-shot.
options.text: The wolves. Say what you need.

options._comment: #396 REPORT ROWS (3): each requires heard_winter_teeth BESIDE its route counter (survived_wolf_night banks quest-free at river_wolf_pack on_victory) so no ungated producer leaks winter_answered.
options.text: We stood the night. The pack's thinner for it.
The fold's rebuilt. Double hurdles, drained ground.
Your wolves were pushed. Something holds their old ground.

thicket_brief.speaker: A Shepherd
thicket_brief.text: Corusdeer. Whole herd came down off the north road. Stopped dead at the old line in the thicket. Wouldn't cross. Wouldn't spook. Turned and walked back the way they came. Something taught this herd that line. Two lambs I lost this spring. Something with thorns for teeth took them. So no. I'm not walking in there on my own.

thicket_sign.speaker: A Shepherd
thicket_sign.text: Here. Hoof marks come up, stop, turn, go back. Same line, every time. You can't see it from standing. Not one print past it in a mile of treeline. Teeth would've left a mess. There's no mess.

effects.toast: You spend the afternoon on it. Two rails down, re-set forty paces east, and the herd's road runs through the gap by dusk.

thicket_rerouted.speaker: A Shepherd
thicket_rerouted.text: So you spend the afternoon on it. Two fence lines down, re-set forty paces east. Word goes round the fields before dusk. The herd keeps its road for the winter. I walk the new line twice before I trust it.

thicket_topic.speaker: A Shepherd
thicket_topic.text: Know that treeline better than the headman does. He'd rather not. There's a hut the far side of the hollow. Nobody's opened it in years. Whoever kept it drew that line. You're the reading sort? Start there.

thicket_reported_read.speaker: A Shepherd
thicket_reported_read.text: A ward. Somebody scratched a line in the dirt a hundred years back. The deer still stop at it. Grass grown right over the scratch by now. First real thing anyone's told me about that thicket. The rest was guesses.

thicket_reported_rerouted.speaker: A Shepherd
thicket_reported_rerouted.text: Fences before deer. My father would have said the same and then done the opposite. Herd's watering at the north bend now. Where I can see them. I'll sleep better for it. Haven't lately.

thicket_reported_cleared.speaker: A Shepherd
thicket_reported_cleared.text: Denning right on the line, of course it was. Well, it's dead now. Line's still there and the deer still won't cross it. One thing learned, then. Lambs go back on the near field tomorrow.

winter_brief.speaker: A Shepherd
winter_brief.text: Stand the watch with me and we thin them. Or the hurdles are cut for a new fold. That's the two I've got. Wolves don't move ground for nothing.

winter_topic.speaker: A Shepherd
winter_topic.text: Hurdles are stacked by the pen. The watch is mine, every night. And the sign. I near forgot the sign. Runs the west margin, plain as a road. Walk it back and you'd know what pushed them.

watch_agreed._comment: banks hunter_will_come (FROZEN id): NPC fields as ally at river_wolf_pack. effects+end:true fires DIALOGUE_ENDED before the effect (carried from legacy `agreed`).
watch_agreed.speaker: A Shepherd
watch_agreed.text: Field edge, after dark. Bring your own bandages. I've got enough of my own to worry about.

winter_reported_watch.speaker: A Shepherd
winter_reported_watch.text: So we did. That's one night. Another comes tomorrow. I'll stand that too.

winter_reported_fold.speaker: A Shepherd
winter_reported_fold.text: Walked it this morning. Gate hangs true. A wolf tests a fence once and remembers. My father built the old fold. This one's dug deeper and the ground's drained.

winter_reported_traced.speaker: A Shepherd
winter_reported_traced.text: Pushed. Off their own ground, by the old line. So it was never my fields they wanted. Wolves and me both, working round something neither of us can see.
